baseline.note: This fixture records pressure against the pre-M1 model. It is evidence for later design work, not a replacement methodology.

attacks.scenario: Case A has repeated independent attestations but no evidence of institutionalization. Case B has one unusually rich legal/administrative corpus establishing an institutional category but uncertain prevalence.
attacks.current_representation: P1-P4 is one ordered practice_level field; P1/P2 chiefly encode evidentiary configuration while P3/P4 encode institutional/structural historical characterization.
attacks.strongest_simpler_defense: Keep P0-P4 and clarify the legend; users can read the definitions.
attacks.discriminating_reason: The two cases cannot be ordered on one historical quantity without choosing which construct the ordering means. This affects storage, sorting, aggregation and map color, not wording alone.

attacks.scenario: A claim has completed specialist review and remains genuinely disputed. Another completed review is researched-inconclusive.
attacks.current_representation: coverage_state is one field containing workflow-like values (not_researched, source_identified, reviewed, classified) and outcome-like values (disputed, researched_inconclusive).
attacks.strongest_simpler_defense: Treat disputed and researched_inconclusive as terminal workflow stages.
attacks.discriminating_reason: Review completion and epistemic outcome can both be true simultaneously; one field cannot answer both questions without losing state.

attacks.scenario: The surviving Silla register has proposed dates across 695-819 CE; the record itself says this interval must not be read as a 125-year continuous observation.
attacks.current_representation: claim.from_year/to_year and valid_years supply the query interval, with temporal_precision/certainty as metadata.
attacks.strongest_simpler_defense: The UI can show the disputed date label while the database keeps one interval.
attacks.discriminating_reason: A selected-year query inside that interval can return a claim even though the interval expresses possible dating rather than continuous validity. This changes query truth conditions, not merely display.

attacks.scenario: Evidence concerns four village-register communities associated with the Seowon-gyeong/Cheongju area; it must not become a claim about all Unified Silla territory.
attacks.current_representation: spatial_precision is free text and the territorial-practice claim points to one spatial_entity; geometry may be unresolved as a safeguard.
attacks.strongest_simpler_defense: Keep narrow spatial entities and rely on editorial discipline; no new semantics are needed.
attacks.discriminating_reason: The current case demonstrates good editorial restraint, but the model cannot separately query evidence locus versus justified inference extent or enforce the rationale for a larger fill.

attacks.scenario: Baekje's 369 record supports a bounded capture/distribution/enslavement event without independently establishing prevalence across Baekje society.
attacks.current_representation: The event is stored as a TERRITORIAL_PRACTICE_CLAIM with practice_type_code slavery_enslavement and P1.
attacks.strongest_simpler_defense: P1 plus a one-year interval already communicates that the event is bounded.
attacks.discriminating_reason: Event/process and social-status/practice are different predicates. Queries for territorial slavery currently retrieve the event through the same subtype, so this is not only a label problem.

attacks.scenario: The Hittite case simultaneously concerns an enslaved status/category, property/pricing rules, herding function and status flexibility.
attacks.strongest_simpler_defense: Put secondary characteristics in notes and keep one headline category.
attacks.discriminating_reason: Characteristics needed for cross-society comparison become unqueryable prose and mutually exclusive codes force a false choice. Multiple facets are part of the analytical claim.

attacks.scenario: Mauryan evidence contains supporting, challenging and qualifying sources while the reviewed synthesis reaches a positive bounded working designation.
attacks.current_representation: CLAIM_SOURCE directions coexist on one claim and coverage/classification need not become disputed merely because evidence conflicts.
attacks.strongest_attack: Conflicting evidence should force separate competing claims or an unresolved classification.
attacks.discriminating_reason: The case preserves counterevidence and still records a transparent working synthesis, matching the project's evidence-synthesis purpose without losing provenance.

attacks.scenario: The evidence spans multiple Maya polities and sites and must not be rendered as one Maya empire or maximum extent.
attacks.current_representation: The research region remains distinct from a polity and geometry is explicitly unresolved.
attacks.strongest_attack: A map-first product will pressure the project to invent one convenient polygon.
attacks.discriminating_reason: The existing model already allows a useful historical claim with unresolved geometry and retains neutral land, so missing geometry does not require invented spatial certainty.
